faqs.q: Sec. 74-167. - Site assessment prior to preliminary plat or development plan.
faqs.a:
The city may require a Phase I site assessment be performed on property located within
               the city at the owner's expense, at the time a preliminary plat or development plan
               is submitted by the owner to the city for review when based on physical examination
               of the property or because of information or records brought to its attention, the
               city has a reasonable belief that a condition of environmental contamination by hazardous
               substances exists which may affect the health, safety, or welfare of persons living
               in or working at or residing in or traveling through the proposed development area.
(1)
If a condition of environmental contamination is revealed by the Phase I assessment,
                  the owner shall, at owner's expense, perform a Phase II assessment if owner continues
                  to seek approval by the city of owner's development plan. If the Phase II assessment
                  indicates that a Phase III assessment is necessary, owner shall perform, at owner's
                  expense, a Phase III assessment if owner continues to seek approval of a development
                  plan.
(2)
The city shall not approve any final plat or development plan which has not provided
                  for remediation of known hazardous substance discovered or revealed by an assessment.
                  Remediation of hazardous substances shall be to a satisfactory level and in compliance
                  with standards established by the Environmental Protection Agency, the Colorado Department
                  of Public Health and Environment and the city.
(Code 1981, § 25-86; Ord. No. 3009, § 1, 10-4-1993)
